newsitem.title: EGYPT: Medinet trade boosts Egypt bourse volume.
newsitem.headline: Medinet trade boosts Egypt bourse volume.

text.p: Egyptian share prices weakened a fraction in heavyweight trade in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development shares on Sunday, the first day a new method to calculate bourse closing prices went into effect.
The Capital Market Authority index slipped 0.63 points to 334.6 in good trade of 62.9 million pounds ($18.5 million).
More than 105,000 shares worth 25 million pounds changed hands in Medinet Nasr. Its share rose 1.94 to 239.94 pounds.
Egypt last week issued a decree which changed the way closing prices are calculated on the stock exchange.
The new way of calculating is based on the weighted average of trades in the share throughout the day, excluding the odd lot trades, or those less than 100 shares as volume.
This way, the closing price reflects performance throughout the day, rather than just its activity at the end.
"Basically it's a much more fair system. It reflects the fair value of the stock. Prior to this some companies used to control the prices," said Sarah Gamal, broker at EFG Hermes.

She said she expected the new price calculation system, technical upgrades and the automatic matching system which took effect this month to encourage foreign investors to increase their portfolios in Egypt.
More than 53,000 Commercial International Bank/CIB shares worth 3.9 million pounds changed hands. They closed down 0.07 at 72.68.
"CIB has been doing high volume, close to 100,000 shares, in the past three or four (trading) days," said Gamal.

Mills as a sector were popular. "Today there was volume in mills in general," she said. "There were large volumes today considering what they did last week, when prices dropped and nobody wanted to sell."
North Cairo Flour Mills slipped a fraction, falling 0.02 to 172.98 pounds in two million pounds volume.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 445.75 points from 446.89 points on Thursday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 250.83 from 251.23.
Of the 78 shares traded, 28 rose, 31 ended lower and 19 remained unchanged.
